name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 can propel the bike on its own but can't assist past 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph (23 V.S.A. §4(46))
Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts (23 V.S.A. §4(46))
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512), and the motor disengages or stops when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
A Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently affix a label in at least 9-point Arial stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
Riders under 16 may not ride a Class 3, but may ride as a passenger on one designed to carry passengers (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including highways, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths, with the same rights and duties as a bicyclist (23 V.S.A. §1136a)

A municipality, local authority or state agency may ban Class 1 or Class 2 from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons, and may ban Class 3 from one without a hearing (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the municipality or agency that manages it may regulate e-bike use (23 V.S.A. §1136a)
Not a motor vehicle: exempt from registration, inspection, title, operator's license, insurance and ATV requirements (23 V.S.A. §§4(46), 1136a)

A bicycle with an electric motor of up to 1,000 watts and a top motor speed of 20 mph that isn't an electric bicycle is a motor-assisted bicycle instead, which can't be ridden on sidewalks or by anyone under 16 on a highway
